2022: BBC was invited to participate in the development process of Family Planning Costed Implementation Plan by FP and RH Section of Family Welfare Division

2023 (second half): (1)On Dec. 10, Ministry of Youth and Sport as well National Youth Council (NYC) invited BYAN to provide inputs on the preliminary draft of National Youth Policy in the workshop organized by Ministry of Youth and Sport at Hotel Araniko, Dhulikhel ; (2) On Oct. 08 and 09, Blind Youth Association Nepal was invited to provide inputs and recommendations in the five-year Costed Implementation Plan (CIP) of FP/SRHR program organized by the Family Welfare Division (FWD). Also, On Dec. 31, it was invited by the Family Welfare Division to on the Consultative Meeting for the Adolescent Health and Development Implementation Plan at Hotel Square, Lalitpur with the objective of providing critical feedback from the disability perspectives. (3) On Oct. 30, FP2030 invited BYAN to share its updates on Family Planning Initiatives. 2024: (1) Ministry of Women, Children and Senior Citizen invited BBC during finalisation process of B+30 National Report, (2) National Health Education Information Communication Center invited BBC during finalisation of Menstruation Package, (3) National Health Education Information Communication Center invited BBC during mapping and discussion development of Disability Friendly Health Education materials

description.narrative: # of advocacy initiatives carried by CSOs for, by or with their constituencies at sub-national level

comment.narrative: 2021: No advocacy initiatives2022: Provincial Level Youth Consultation for country call to action for APFSD 2023: This includes advocacy meetings with provincial level government stakeholders, and provincial consultations for UPR midterm report, amongst others.

2023 (second half): Total 6. This includes lobby meeting with provincial government and local governments, technical support to a municipality on local curriculum development, etc.2024: Total 22. This includes, lobby meeting with several municipalities and sub-metros on budget allocation, prioritisation of SRHR programmes at local level, and queer inclusive policies.

title.narrative: 3.2.1 Number of advocacy initiatives carried out by CSOs for, by or with their constituencies at national, regional or international level

description.narrative: # of advocacy initiatives carried out by CSOs for, by or with their constituencies at all other levels

comment.narrative: 2021: There were 7 national level advocacy initiatives focusing on meetings and lobbying towards state actors. A few examples include: lobby and consultation with the CDC on the adoption of a comprehensive curriculum when it comes to sexuality education, lobby meeting with CEHRD on the adoption and implementation of CSE monitoring framework, consultation with the government on the implementation of CEDAW recommendations related to Article 12.2022: CSE advocacy coalition; and MoU with CEHRD2023: This includes advocacy meetings with FWD team, HEICC, joint advocacy dialogues, public litagation for marriage equality etc.

2023 (second half): Total 12. This includes annual consultative meetings with CDC and CEHRD, CS training for school nurses, consultation workshop for development call to action for APPC.2024: Total 22. This includes meetings with Ministry of Women Children and Senior Citizens, Development and promotion of IEC materials, National ICPD+30 consultation, Meetings with CDC, cEHRD and NHEICC regarding CSE curriculum and materials.
